original_question: Is the gene associated with Xeroderma pigmentosum (XP), which can cause trichothiodystrophy when mutated, located on chromosome 19?

final_qi.question: Is the gene associated with Xeroderma pigmentosum (XP), which can cause trichothiodystrophy when mutated, located on chromosome 19?
final_qi.long_answer: Yes. The ERCC2 gene—also known as XPD—is situated at chromosome 19q13.2-q13.3. Pathogenic variants in ERCC2 cause Xeroderma pigmentosum complementation group D, and certain missense or truncating mutations in the same gene lead to trichothiodystrophy. Thus, the XP-associated gene whose mutation can produce trichothiodystrophy is indeed located on chromosome 19.
